commit.message:
feat(tools): export and import the document's tools as a tool library file

The Tool library page gains "Export library..." and "Import library...".
Export writes every document tool as camcraft-tools/1 JSON ({format,
version, units: mm, tools: [{name, definition}]}), each definition the
exact tool shape MCP's get_job/add_tool and the project file already use.
Import (app::tool_library::parse_tool_library + commands::ImportTools) is
one undo unit: the whole file is validated first - malformed JSON, a
wrong format/version, a missing field, a name twice, a reserved name or a
tool Tool::is_sane refuses each refuse the import by tool name with
nothing applied. A name already in the document is never overwritten: an
identical tool is skipped, a different one comes in as "<name> (2)".
Vendor library formats stay out of scope (clean-room).

Refs #300

feat(tools): judge a modelled tool body by its revolved envelope

A tool can carry a holder/assembly mesh (STEP, STL, OBJ through the model
importer), placed in the tool frame by a model axis direction and the
origin's height above the tip, as one undoable command (SetToolBody:
set / replace / clear). Its revolved envelope - per band along the axis,
the farthest the body reaches, every facet clipped exactly to each band -
is what the stack laws judge:

- the fixture laws (c2)/(d2), prismatic and posed, sweep the body's bands
  in place of the holder cylinder (HolderStack; the cylinder stack keeps
  the old sums, so a tool without a body is bit-identical);
- every one-cylinder law (rest reach, solid law, multi-axis dodge, drill
  reach, machine tool length) reads the cylinder enclosing the body,
  which can only over-report.

Degenerate, non-finite, flat, off-axis, below-tip, oversized and
into-the-flutes bodies refuse by name, at the command, at ChangeTool,
at generation and on load. The body rides the op stamp only when present,
survives DeleteTool/DeleteEntity undo, and saves as an optional `body`
on the tool row (project v54: an old reader must refuse rather than
judge the smaller cylinder).

Fixes #368

fix(tools): an exported tool library always carries the .camtools suffix

Hands-on finding (macOS): the save panel suggests tools.camtools, but a
typed name without a suffix was written as is - macOS does not enforce
an unknown extension - so the library landed with no suffix. Export now
appends .camtools when the chosen name has no extension; a name that
already has one (.camtools, or a deliberate .json) is kept as typed.

Pinned by tool_library::an_export_name_without_a_suffix_gets_the_library_extension.

Refs #300

feat(ui): import, place and pick a tool body in the tool editor; draw it in the simulation

The tool editor gains a Body column: Import body… (STEP/STL/OBJ) and
Clear body, the axis (six presets or a picked face normal), the tip
offset, Pick tip / Pick axis on an egui-painted orbitable 3D preview,
a live placement note, and Apply body, which queues one SetToolBody
(undoable; refusals land on the Tool pane by name). Picks and orbit are
ephemeral. The profile preview overlays the placed body's envelope.

While the simulation runs, the running tool's body is posed at the
playhead and drawn as a model part; tools without a body add nothing.

App helpers live in app::tool_body_view (load, presets, preview, pick,
tip offset, posing, body of an operation's tool).

Fixes #371

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(ui): draw the whole tool in the simulation when it has a body, and frame it

On a real document the body was posed a shank length above the tip
with nothing below it, off the top of a part-framed view, so the
simulation looked the same with and without it. A tool with a body now
draws whole while simulating - cutter and shank revolved from its
numbers up into the body (app::tool_body_view::assembly) - at every
playhead, paused or playing, stale or fresh; Frame takes the posed
assembly in. Tools without a body draw exactly as before.

Pinned on the user's own document (step_block_371.camproj fixture).

Refs #371

feat(ui): zoom and fit the tool editor's 3D body preview

Wheel or pinch (Ctrl+wheel) over the preview zooms about the cursor,
clamped to 1/4x..32x of the fit view; double-click or the new Fit
button resets orbit, zoom and pan. Drag still orbits. View state only.
The decision file records the zoom and the whole-tool simulation
drawing.

Refs #371

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(ui): the simulation draws the tool and its holder cylinder when it has no body

The running tool is now always drawn at the playhead: cutter and shank
revolved from Tool::profile, then the modelled body when it has one,
else the holder cylinder from its own numbers (holder_d x holder_len on
the shank top - the HolderStack::cylinder reading the collision laws
judge). The lathe insert kinds keep the axis marker only: their profile
is a stand-in envelope. Tests and the decision file follow.

Refs #371
